title: large-both-streams
setup: Create a fresh short Unix socket path and an empty lifetime-lock directory in test-owned temporary storage; set L_PHASE1_SOCKET and L_PHASE1_DIRECTORY for the orchestrator. Start the controller before the program.
Each child has its own connection. Parse a complete ready <label> <pid> line and reject duplicate/unexpected labels. Record direct PIDs separately from controller and orchestrator.
Controller commands are exactly release followed by LF; readiness does not release a child. Test deadlines bound failures only.

Keep every controller connection open until runtime shutdown has been observed. Require spontaneous child disconnection and lifetime-lock release before controller closure or fallback signals; record cleanup failures before fallback. Lock release alone does not prove direct-child reaping.

Wait for ready x (sent after both 262144-byte writes finish) and ready gate before releasing Gate. Require drained| on orchestrator stdout before releasing Worker. Keep output readers active throughout.
assertions: Exact stdout is drained| followed by 262144 ASCII x bytes; orchestrator stderr is empty.
Worker completes both large writes while orchestrator is in Gate's Execute, before its own source Await. No source-level channel or generated companion replacement is used.
Use the paired native runtime test to assert exact captured stderr (262144 ASCII e bytes) and streaming capture state; L does not expose stderr.

Native backpressure variants choose payload larger than measured pipe capacity. This fixed-size integration fixture exercises ordinary-host large capture without asserting a universal kernel pipe-size ceiling.
